name: IEC dynamic input (edge-triggered)
summary: Wedge drawn inside the outline at an input, meaning the input acts on a transition rather than a level.
description: The dynamic input indicator is a small wedge inside the outline at the point where the input line enters. It means the input is active only on a transition, normally from external 0 to 1 in positive logic. It is the mark that distinguishes an edge-triggered flip-flop clock from a level-sensitive latch enable.

On sequential logic drawings the reader should look for the wedge at every C input. A missing wedge on a clock input changes the device from edge-triggered to transparent, which changes timing behaviour significantly.

The wedge does not specify setup or hold time, nor maximum clock rate. Those are device timing parameters. Check the active clock edge against the input waveform and the timing data of the actual logic element.
readingNotes: Wedge present: edge-triggered; wedge absent: level-sensitive.
Check for a negation or polarity mark that reverses the active edge.
drawingChecklist: Draw the wedge inside the outline at the clock input.
Show negation outside the outline for falling-edge inputs.
Label the input with its dependency number, for example C1.
distinction: The postponed-output mark relates to pulse-triggered elements whose output changes at the end of the pulse, not at the edge.
